title: European robin
label: Robin, 14 cm
blurb: A European robin, about 14 cm long, standing alert on a boulder. Zoom right in: it is built to true size. Click any part, or use the layer buttons.
model_note: A model built from typical proportions of an adult robin (about 14 cm long, 16 to 22 g), not a scan of one bird. The overall size and the feather counts that are published (10 primaries, 9 secondaries, 12 tail feathers) are used; every other proportion, and the size and place of every organ, is drawn by eye from photographs and anatomical drawings and is approximate. The bird stands still; the feathers are drawn as simple blades.

legend.title: On the cut face
legend.note: The bird is cut along its midline: look at it from its right side first, then press the button. A schematic section: the pale pink between the organs is a stand-in for fat and connective tissue, not a scan.

legend.note: Look at the bird from its right side, then press the button: the cut passes along the right wing. The bones are drawn as simple rods; the muscles are schematic.

legend.note: Drawn at true size (the windpipe is a few millimetres wide), simplified: the real membranes, rings and muscles are more complex. Look at the bird from the front, then press the button.

legend.title: In the eye
legend.note: A model eye about 8 mm across, with a schematic layout. Look at the bird from the front, then press the button.

legend.title: In the heart
legend.note: A simplified model heart: chamber shapes and wall thicknesses are schematic. Look at the bird from above, then press the button.
